correctness.rationale: For a fixed label-two support H in K_n with t edges, the exact best weight is N_n+t-ab, where a and b count root vertices of degree zero and one: an edge outside H sees d_H(u)+d_H(v) defenders and all ab eligible edges must be zero at optimum. Let c=n−a−b. If c>0 and b is even, 2t≥b+2c makes ab−t at least c(b+1) below the value Q_n(b)=b(n−b)−b/2 from a matching on b vertices. If b is odd, integrality gives an extra 1/2 loss; b−1 and b+1 are feasible even sizes and the two changes from Q_n(b) sum to −2, so one matching loses at most 1 and still strictly wins. Thus every optimum support is a matching. The matching weight is N_n+4r²+(1−2n)r, with unique nearest feasible integer to (2n−1)/8, namely floor((2n+3)/8); no ties occur because 2n−1 is odd. The labels are forced by the conditional optimum, so counting labelled partial pairings gives exactly the factorial formula. This covers n=3 and the entire permitted range. An independent direct original-adjacency check agreed for all supports through n=6, also testing every ternary labelling through n=5.
residual_risks: The finite check corroborates but does not establish the all-n theorem. The proof concerns standard vertex perfect Roman domination, not the neighborhood-label-sum variant.

value.rationale: Triangular graphs are a canonical highly symmetric family, and imposing uniqueness of the defending neighbor changes the order of the minimum from ordinary Roman’s linear value to quadratic. The degree-class argument proves an actual rigidity result, not just an example giving the optimal weight: every optimizer has a unique matching support with a forced labelling. This yields an exact count usable independently of the scalar parameter and identifies why ordinary-Roman polynomial information is inadequate.
residual_risks: The result does not enumerate all perfect Roman functions or treat arbitrary line graphs.
